COD.note: The ADN only pleads for a future regulatory framework on AI governance; no draft or rule is stated.
Nothing on AI in use in government bodies.
Nothing on AI inside a sector's public system.

facts.fact: The ADN's first deputy coordinator spoke at the closing of a workshop on 4 August 2026 in Kinshasa that validated the Stratégie nationale de l'Intelligence artificielle (SNIA), with four pillars; no adoption by the government is stated.

COD.note: No body or funding tied to the strategy is stated; the ADN says it is not the executing body.
Compute infrastructure is named only as a strategy pillar, nothing built or in service.

facts.fact: The Politique sectorielle de l'Économie numérique 2026-2030 was presented for validation at a workshop closed on 4 August 2026 in Kinshasa, the ADN says; no adoption by the government is stated.
The Politique sectorielle de l'Économie numérique is dated 2026-2030, the document gives.

The ADN's first deputy coordinator gave the closing review of the 2019 Plan national du numérique: overall operationalisation 64%, 17 of 44 projects completed and 27 in operationalisation, with a public funding shortfall cited.

COD.note: The policy is described as a digital economy policy, not an ICT or telecoms sector policy; held under digitalstrategy.
ADN gives support to government but no system run or built by staff is stated.
Startups are mentioned only as an aim of the AI strategy; no law, label or fund.
No hub or park is mentioned.
